question.leadin: This man was shot and killed by a Union soldier after the barn where he was hiding was set on fire.
question.text: Name this stage actor who shouted "Sic semper tyrannis" as he assassinated Abraham Lincoln.
question.clue: Samuel Mudd created a splint for this man's broken leg.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a defunct Cabinet position.
swap.text: This member of Franklin Pierce's cabinet later became the first and only president of the Confederate States of America.
swap.clue: Cornelius Vanderbilt and Horace Greeley helped secure the $100,000 bond for the release of this man, who was advised by Judah P. Benjamin and Alexander Stephens while holding the highest office of a country defended by Robert E. Lee.

question.text: This chief justice for the case wrote "a negro, whose ancestors were imported into America and sold as slaves," would never be a citizen even if freed and had no right to sue in U.S. Courts.
question.clue: After replacing William Duane, he ordered the end of federal deposits into the Second Bank of the United States as Secretary of the Treasury, but Jackson's bid to replace Gabriel Duvall with this man was a failure.

swap.text: This May 2-4, 1862 battle in Virginia saw the Union under Gen. Hooker defeated by the Confederates, under Gen. Lee. It was notable as the site of the death of Thomas "Stonewall" Jackson.
swap.clue: Occurring at the intersection of the Orange Plank Road and Orange Turnpike, it saw Early man Marye's Heights to isolate Sedgwick.

question.text: The issue of slavery in the new territories prompted the signing of this agreement, which saw California admitted as a free state and the establishment of popular sovereignty for deciding whether or not a territory would allow slavery.
question.clue: Texas agreed to place its northern border at 36o30' and relinquished its claims to New Mexico.

swap.leadin: Name some important politicians of the mid-19th century.
swap.text: This Republican ran against Buchanan and Fillmore in the 1856 election. Known as "The Pathfinder", he had captured Sonoma in 1846 to form a short-lived California republic with William B. Ide.
swap.clue: Solomon Nunes Carvalho took daguerrotypes for this man, who names a cottonwood that marked water sources on the Old Spanish Trail.

question.leadin: After the Civil War, this man served as the governor of Rhode Island.
question.text: Name this Union general who was famous for his namesake facial hair.
question.clue: This first president of the NRA led the failed Mud March in an attempt to capture Richmond.

swap.leadin: Name some things about trains and the Civil War.
swap.text: A.P. Hill's Confederates beat back Burnside's attack and saved the day at this battle after rushing over from taking the critical railroad bridge at Harper's Ferry. The Emancipation Proclamation was announced after this battle.
swap.clue: The carnage during this conflict earned a sunken road the moniker "Bloody Lane."

question.leadin: Answer the following about an American history.
question.text: Many Northern Know Nothings went back to the Republican Party after this 1856 Supreme Court case that declared Congress to have no power to prohibit slavery in the territories.
question.clue: Grounds for this suit came from John Emerson's move to Wisconsin with the plaintiff.

swap.text: The actions of Fremont in California and Stephen Kearny in New Mexico contributed to this President's success waging the Mexican-American war. This Tennessean won the election of 1844 against Henry Clay.
swap.clue: Congressman Abraham Lincoln opposed this President in the Spot Resolutions.

question.text: This 1862 act, named for a Senator from Vermont, started the tradition of agricultural and mechanical colleges around the United States, often financed with the sale of public property.
question.answerHtml: Morrill Land-Grant Act of 1862 [or Land-Grant College Act of 1862]
question.clue: Lyman Trumbull was initially asked to be the sponsor for this bill by the man sometimes given credit for its introduction, Jonathan Turner, but he instead supported a Vermont Representative as this bill's sponsor.

swap.text: Other early works about domesticity were written by Catharine from this family. Anti-slavery preachers like Lyman and Henry Ward were members of this family, which nicknamed firearms called "[this family's] Bibles."
swap.answerHtml: Beecher family [accept Catharine Beecher; accept Lyman Beecher; accept Henry Ward Beecher; accept Beecher’s Bibles]
swap.clue: Another member of this family used the New England Emigrant Aid Society to ship supplies for use against the Border Ruffians: Sharps Rifles known as his namesake "bibles."

question.text: The last major action before the battle of Shiloh was Grant's capture of these two forts, one on the Tennessee River and one on the Cumberland.
question.clue: Grant earned the nickname "Unconditional Surrender" after forcing John Floyd, Simon Bolivar Buckner, and Gideon Pillow to give up this Tennessee fort.

swap.leadin: Edward Ferrero's United States Colored Troops suffered heavily in the aftermath of this battle, since they were inadequately trained for an experimental assault.
swap.text: Name this 1864 Civil War battle that Ulysses Grant called "the saddest affair I have witnessed in this war." It took place during the Petersburg campaign.
swap.clue: Many of Ferrero's men, sent in to restore order, were executed or returned to slavery by the victors, who were led by a future Readjuster Party senator from Virginia, William Mahone.

question.text: At the opening of the 1858 campaign, Abraham Lincoln gave a speech using this metaphor about the difficulties of the dichotomy between free and slave states. Lincoln claimed that this metaphorical object would become "all one thing, or all the other."
question.clue: This speech suggested that "Stephen, Franklin, Roger, and James" worked together to create a frame, and was the subject of a July 9th response delivered in Chicago by Stephen Douglas.

swap.text: The Taney Court's pro-slavery orientation was reversed under this chief justice who succeeded him. This man also served as Abraham Lincoln's treasury secretary.
swap.clue: This man wrote that the Supreme Court could not issue an injunction against the President after Mississippi asked it to, aiding the beginning of Reconstruction.

question.leadin: Answer the following about members of the Cherokee people.
question.text: Stand Watie [WAY-tee] and his Cherokee Mounted Rifles fought during the Confederate capture of Foster's Farm in this battle. However, Union forces under Samuel Curtis prevailed at this battle to secure control of Missouri and northern Arkansas.

swap.leadin: He was referred to as the "Nestor of the Senate" during his late years in office, and declined to serve as secretary of the treasury under Rutherford B. Hayes.
swap.text: Name this American politician who wrote the book Self-Consciousness of Noted Persons, and who served for almost 32 years after being elected to the Senate in 1866.
swap.clue: One year after passing a namesake protectionist tariff, this politician targeted Mormons by authoring an 1862 Anti-Bigamy Act.

question.leadin: During this battle, Daniel McCook was killed as he shouted "Surrender, you traitors!" at the Dead Angle.
question.text: Name this tactical loss for the Union, the largest frontal assault by William Sherman against Confederates during the Atlanta Campaign.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Civil War general Henry Warner Slocum.
swap.text: Slocum was highly criticized for his tardy arrival at one battle, which earned him the nickname "Slow Come." His defenders cite the fact that Slocum was merely following the cautious "Pipe Creek Circular" issued by this Union general. This man went on to fight the Bristoe Campaign against Robert E. Lee.
swap.clue: During his feud with Daniel Sickles, who nearly cost him his most famous victory, this man was accused of inactivity similar to that he showed at Mine Run.
